definition_zh: 漠不关心的；冷淡的；平庸的
definition_en: not interested in or caring about something, or not especially good
core_image: 一个人坐在雨里看报，衣服湿透了也不抬头
scene: 投票那天，最怕听到的一句话是「都一样」。Most young people are indifferent to local elections.
sceneCN: 这里 indifferent 是「漠不关心」（第 1 个义项：不感兴趣、不在意）；句意是多数年轻人对地方选举漠不关心。

pos.zh: 形容词：漠不关心的；冷淡的；平庸的

derivatives.zh: 义为「冷漠、漠然」，由本词加 -ence 构成
义为「冷淡地；平平地」
义为「不同的」，与本词同根
义为「不同、相异」

senses.title: Not caring about something
senses.titleCN: 漠不关心：对该在意的事不在意
senses.definition: having no interest in or sympathy for something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事没有兴趣或同情
senses.example: Most young people are indifferent to local elections.
senses.exampleCN: 多数年轻人对地方选举漠不关心。
senses.why: The Latin word means making no difference, and a person who feels no difference does not care.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在拉丁语里意为「不造成差别」，而感觉不出差别的人自然就不关心。

senses.title: Unmoved by praise or blame
senses.titleCN: 无动于衷：不为褒贬所动
senses.definition: not influenced or excited by something that moves others
senses.definitionCN: 不被能打动他人的事物所影响或激起
senses.example: He seemed indifferent to fame.
senses.exampleCN: 他似乎对名声无动于衷。
senses.why: Stoic calm and coldness share the same shape, so the word can praise or blame.
senses.whyCN: 淡泊与冷淡形状相同，因此这个词既可用于褒也可用于贬。

senses.title: Neither good nor bad
senses.definition: of only average quality, nothing special
senses.definitionCN: 质量只属一般，没有特别之处
senses.example: The food was indifferent but cheap.
senses.exampleCN: 饭菜平平，但便宜。
senses.why: If something makes no difference to you, it is neither impressive nor bad.
senses.whyCN: 如果某物对你造不成差别，它就既不出色也不糟糕。

senses.title: In science, having no effect
senses.titleCN: 无影响的：科学中不产生作用
senses.definition: in older scientific use, producing no effect or not varying
senses.definitionCN: 在旧式科学用语中，指不产生效果或不变化
senses.example: An indifferent gas does not react with the mixture.
senses.exampleCN: 惰性气体不与混合物反应。
senses.why: A substance that makes no difference to a reaction earns the same word as a careless person.
senses.whyCN: 对反应不起作用的物质与人所得的评价，竟是同一个词。

intro.en: Indifferent is in-, not, plus different, from Latin differre, to carry apart, to differ.
intro.cn: indifferent 是 in-（不）加 different，后者源自拉丁语 differre「分开携带、相异」。

items.en: Differre meant to carry apart and, by extension, to differ.
items.cn: differre 意为分开携带，引申为「相异」。

items.en: Indifferens meant making no difference between things, neither this nor that.
items.cn: indifferens 意为「不作区分」，既非此也非彼。

items.en: English first used it for undecided or neutral matters such as taste.
items.cn: 英语最初用它形容口味之类无关紧要、无可无不可的事。

items.en: The word shifted from neutral to not caring, a colder judgement.
items.cn: 词义从「中性」滑向「不关心」，评价变得更冷。

items.en: It kept the older sense of ordinary quality in phrases such as indifferent food.
items.cn: 在 indifferent food 这类说法里，它保留了「质量一般」的旧义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the differ- root; the near-meaning group holds words for coldness of feeling.
note.cn: 形近组共用 differ- 词根；近义组收表示感情冷淡的词。

entries.definition: Not the same as another.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不同的」，去掉 in- 即成。

entries.definition: A lack of interest or concern.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「冷漠、漠然」。

entries.definition: In a cold or mediocre way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「冷淡地；平平地」。

entries.definition: Not worried or interested.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不关心的、不在意的」。

entries.definition: Showing no friendly feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「冷淡的」，更口语。

entries.definition: Separate and not emotionally involved.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「超然的、抽离的」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the no-difference reading, the neutral-to-cold shift and the mediocre meal.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「无差别」的字面义、由中性转冷淡的漂移与那顿平庸的饭。

normal.en: In plus different: if nothing is different to you, you do not care which one happens.
normal.cn: in 加 different：什么对你都一样，你就不在意发生哪一个。

normal.en: Being indifferent is not the same as being different; one word means the difference has vanished.
normal.cn: indifferent 不是 different：前者说的是差别消失了。

normal.en: Indifferent food is neither good nor bad, because it makes no difference to your evening.
normal.cn: indifferent food 不好也不坏，因为它对你的这个晚上毫无影响。

normal.en: The noun is indifference, the letter e replaces the final t, like different and difference.
normal.cn: 名词是 indifference，结尾 t 换成 e，正如 different 与 difference。

normal.en: A man reading in the rain is the picture: the world is wet, he is not moved.
normal.cn: 雨里看报的人就是这幅画面：世界湿透了，他毫不动容。

abstract.en: Indifference is freedom from concern, which is either wisdom or irresponsibility.
abstract.cn: 漠然是从牵挂中脱身，它要么是智慧，要么是不负责任。

abstract.en: The opposite of love is not hate but not caring which way things go.
abstract.cn: 爱的反面不是恨，而是不在意事情往哪儿走。

abstract.en: To say something makes no difference is already a decision about it.
abstract.cn: 说某事无关紧要，本身就已经是有关它的一个决定。

examples.en: She was indifferent to the praise and kept working.
examples.cn: 她对赞扬毫不在意，继续工作。

examples.en: The service at the hotel was indifferent.
examples.cn: 那家旅馆的服务很一般。

examples.en: No one can remain indifferent to such suffering.
examples.cn: 面对这样的苦难，没有人能无动于衷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印地分润」——分红时分给谁他都一样，事不关己，便漠不关心。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ differre（分开携带、相异）→ indifferens（不作区分）；同根词有 different、differ、difference、ferry。

sensesIntro.en: Indifferent starts as a statement that no difference is made, turns into not caring, and slides from there into both coldness of feeling and ordinary quality.
sensesIntro.cn: indifferent 起初只是说「不造成差别」，随后变为「不关心」，再由此滑向感情冷淡与质量平平。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone reading a newspaper in the rain, never looking up.
core.cn: 核心意象：有人在雨里看报，从不抬头。

branches.en: APATHY LINE: the outcome no longer matters to someone.
branches.cn: 冷漠线：结果对某人不再重要。

branches.en: STOIC LINE: praise and blame move nobody.
branches.cn: 淡泊线：褒与贬都打不动人。

branches.en: QUALITY LINE: what moves no one is merely average.
branches.cn: 质量线：打不动人的东西也只是平常。

branches.en: CHEMISTRY LINE: a substance that changes nothing.
branches.cn: 化学线：不改变任何东西的物质。

branches.en: JUDGEMENT LINE: the same word praises calm and blames carelessness.
branches.cn: 评判线：同一个词既赞沉静也责疏忽。

intro.en: A negative prefix on a verb meaning to differ, with a participial adjective ending.
intro.cn: 否定前缀加在表示「相异」的动词上，再接分词形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin in-, not, plus differre, to carry apart, plus -ens gave indifferens.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in-「不」加 differre「分开携带」加 -ens，构成 indifferens。

items.example: the root of transfer and refer
items.exampleCN: transfer 与 refer 的词根

definition_zh: 土生土长的；原住民的；本地原产的；当地固有的
definition_en: originating naturally in a particular place, or belonging to the original people of a region
core_image: 一棵树从本地的土里长出来，根就在这里，不在别处
scene: 这里指「土生土长的」。 The reserve protects plants indigenous to the valley, several of which grow nowhere else.
sceneCN: 这里 indigenous 是「本地原产的」（第 2 个义项：某物种自然生长于某地）；句意：保护区保护本山谷原产的植物，其中几种在其他地方完全不生长。图中可辨识物件：山谷轮廓、贴地生长的灌木、标出边界的围栏。

pos.zh: 土生土长的；原住民的；本地原产的

derivatives.zh: 本地人；原住民
原住性；本土性
使本土化
本土化

senses.title: Belonging to the original people
senses.definition: relating to the people who first lived in a region
senses.definitionCN: 与最早居住于某地区的人群相关的
senses.example: The law recognizes indigenous land rights.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法律承认原住民的土地权利。
senses.why: Indigena meant 'born in the place'. The adjective marks people whose origin is in the ground under them, not across a sea.
senses.whyCN: indigena 意为“生在此地”。这个形容词标记的是根在脚下土地而非海外的人。

senses.title: Native to a region's wildlife
senses.definition: in biology, describing a species that evolved naturally in a given area
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中描述在某地区自然演化的物种
senses.example: The garden grows only indigenous shrubs.
senses.exampleCN: 这座花园只种本地原生灌木。
senses.why: A species is indigenous when its line began here. The word is about origin, not about being common.
senses.whyCN: 一个物种若其谱系始于此地，就是本地原产的。这个词讲的是来源，而不是常见与否。

senses.title: Rooted in local culture
senses.definition: describing customs or institutions that developed locally rather than being imported
senses.definitionCN: 描述在当地发展而非输入的风俗或制度
senses.example: The festival is indigenous to the island.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节庆是该岛固有的。
senses.why: Culture is treated like a plant: it grew in this soil, and its roots show it.
senses.whyCN: 文化被当作植物看待：它在这片土壤里长成，根就证明了这一点。

senses.title: Growing from within, not imposed
senses.definition: in development studies, arising from local resources and initiative
senses.definitionCN: 发展研究中由本地资源与主动性产生的
senses.example: They argued for indigenous development rather than imported models.
senses.exampleCN: 他们主张内生发展，而不是照搬外来模式。
senses.why: Here the metaphor is political: what is indigenous grew up here and does not need a scaffold brought from abroad.
senses.whyCN: 这里的比喻是政治性的：内生的东西在这里长成，不需要从国外运来脚手架。

senses.title: A language of the place
senses.definition: describing a language spoken by a region's original inhabitants
senses.definitionCN: 描述由某地区原初居民使用的语言
senses.example: The school teaches two indigenous languages.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校教授两种本地语言。
senses.why: A language is the deepest root a community has. The word says its grammar was formed here.
senses.whyCN: 语言是一个共同体最深的根。这个词说它的语法是在此地形成的。

senses.title: Naturally present in the ground
senses.definition: describing minerals or materials found naturally in a place rather than brought in
senses.definitionCN: 描述在当地天然存在而非输入的材料或矿物
senses.example: The pigment is made from indigenous clay.
senses.exampleCN: 这种颜料由本地黏土制成。
senses.why: The oldest sense is geological: the material was formed under this ground and has never travelled.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是地质性的：材料在这片土地下形成，从未旅行过。

senses.title: Born and raised in the place
senses.definition: describing a person born and raised in a particular region
senses.definitionCN: 描述在某地区出生并长大的人
senses.example: He is indigenous to the highlands.
senses.exampleCN: 他是高地土生土长的人。
senses.why: This is the literal core: a person born in the place. It is neutral about politics and simply states origin.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面核心：生在此地的人。它对政治中立，只陈述来源。

senses.title: Local as opposed to imported
senses.definition: describing what belongs to a place as distinct from what was introduced
senses.definitionCN: 描述属于本地、区别于外来引入的事物
senses.example: Local farmers prefer indigenous breeds.
senses.exampleCN: 当地农民偏爱本地品种。
senses.why: The word always draws a border. On one side are things grown here; on the other, things carried in.
senses.whyCN: 这个词始终画一条边界。一边是在此地长成的东西，另一边是被搬进来的东西。

intro.en: Indigenous comes from Latin indigena, 'a native, one born in the country'. It is built from an old form of in- plus gignere, 'to beget, to give birth'. The word therefore means 'born here', and every sense tests where a thing's origin lies.
intro.cn: indigenous 来自拉丁语 indigena“本地人、本地出生者”。它由 in- 的古体加 gignere“生育、产生”构成。因此这个词意为“在此出生”，每个义项都在检验某物的来源在何处。

items.en: The root behind gignere, 'to beget', is reconstructed as *gen-, 'to give birth, to produce'. It is generally accepted and also underlies genus, generate and kin.
items.cn: gignere“生育”背后的词根被重构为 *gen-“生育、产生”，一般被接受，也是 genus、generate 与 kin 的来源。

items.en: Gignere meant 'to beget, to cause to be'. Its related noun genus named a birth-line or kind. The two words gave English a whole family of origin words.
items.cn: gignere 意为“生育、使存在”。其相关名词 genus 指血统或种类。两个词为英语提供了一整族关于来源的词。

items.en: Indu- is an archaic form of in-, preserved in indigena. The identification of indu- with in- is generally accepted but rests on comparison rather than direct record.
items.cn: indu- 是 in- 的古体，保存在 indigena 中。把 indu- 认定为 in- 一般被接受，但依据是比较而非直接记录。

items.en: Indigena meant 'native, born in the place'. It was used of people, animals and plants alike, which is why the English word covers all three.
items.cn: indigena 意为“本地的、在此出生的”，既用于人，也用于动物与植物，这就是英语这个词同时覆盖三类对象的原因。

items.en: English borrowed indigenous in the 17th century as a learned word for 'native'. Early writers applied it to plants before peoples.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪借入 indigenous 作学术词，意为“本地的”。早期作者先把它用于植物，后用于人群。

items.en: Indigenous peoples became the standard international term for the original inhabitants of a region, carrying legal claims about land and self-government.
items.cn: indigenous peoples 成为国际上指某地区原初居民的标准说法，承载关于土地与自治的法律主张。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the noun for a person, the abstract noun and the verb of making local. The meaning group compares words for belonging to a place.
note.cn: 形近组区分指人的名词、抽象名词与“使本土化”的动词；词义组比较表示“属于某地”的词。

entries.definition: a person or organism native to a region. It is the countable noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 某地区原生的个人或生物。它是形容词背后的可数名词。

entries.definition: the quality of being indigenous. It is used in academic and political writing.
entries.definitionCN: 土生土长的性质。它用于学术与政治写作。

entries.definition: to make something local in character. It is the active form of the adjective's idea.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物具有本地特征。它是形容词观念的活动形式。

entries.definition: belonging to a place by birth. It is the everyday near-synonym and can also mean 'innate'.
entries.definitionCN: 因出生而属于某地。它是日常近义词，也可指“天生的”。

entries.definition: relating to the earliest known inhabitants. It is close to sense 01 but is used especially of Australia and Canada.
entries.definitionCN: 与已知最早居民有关的。它接近第 1 义项，尤用于澳大利亚与加拿大。

entries.definition: found only in one region, often of a species or disease. It stresses restriction, while indigenous stresses origin.
entries.definitionCN: 仅见于某一地区，常用于物种或疾病。它强调限定，而 indigenous 强调来源。

entries.definition: belonging to a particular neighbourhood or district. It is broader and carries no claim about origins.
entries.definitionCN: 属于某一街区或地区的。它更宽，不含关于起源的主张。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build indigenous from indu- plus gignere, 'to be born', and keep the image of a tree whose roots never left this soil.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩从 indu- 加 gignere“生育”搭起 indigenous，并保留“树根从未离开这片土”的意象。

normal.en: See gignere: born. Indigenous means born in this place, not brought here.
normal.cn: 看见 gignere：出生。indigenous 意为在此地出生，而非被搬来。

normal.en: Picture a tree whose roots are visible in the local soil and go nowhere else.
normal.cn: 想象一棵树，根就露在本地土壤里，哪里也不去。

normal.en: Compare with exotic: indigenous grew here, exotic was carried in.
normal.cn: 与 exotic 对照：indigenous 是在此长成，exotic 是被搬进来。

normal.en: An indigenous language keeps its grammar in the ground of the community.
normal.cn: 本地语言把语法留在共同体脚下的土里。

normal.en: Remember the family: genus, generate and native all come from the same 'birth' root.
normal.cn: 记住词族：genus、generate、native 都出自同一个“出生”词根。

abstract.en: Keep one image: a border drawn around a place, and everything inside it that grew there.
abstract.cn: 只记一个意象：围绕某地画一条边界，边界内一切在此长成的东西。

abstract.en: Treat the word as a question about origin, not about quality.
abstract.cn: 把这个词当作关于来源的问题，而不是关于品质的问题。

abstract.en: Notice that the same adjective defends a plant, a language and a legal right.
abstract.cn: 注意同一个形容词可以为一株植物、一种语言和一项法定权利辩护。

examples.en: The museum works closely with indigenous communities.
examples.cn: 这家博物馆与原住民社区密切合作。

examples.en: Several indigenous species are now threatened by the dam.
examples.cn: 几种本地原生种如今受到大坝威胁。

examples.en: The programme supports indigenous knowledge in medicine.
examples.cn: 该项目支持医学领域的本土知识。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“印地真牛死”：印度本地土生土长的牛真厉害——土生土长的、原产的。

root: 拉丁语 indigena“本地出生者”，由 indu-（in- 的古体，“在内”）加 gignere“生育”构成；核心义为“在此地出生、根在此地”。

sensesIntro.en: Indigenous always asks one question: where did this begin? A people, a shrub, a festival, a development strategy, a language, a clay deposit, a person and a breed are all tested against the same border. Whatever grew inside the border is indigenous; whatever was carried across it is not.
sensesIntro.cn: indigenous 始终在问一个问题：这东西起源于哪里？一个民族、一株灌木、一个节庆、一种发展战略、一门语言、一处黏土矿、一个人、一个品种，都用同一条边界来检验。在边界内长成的是 indigenous；被搬过边界进来的不是。

core.en: Born and grown inside a place, with roots that never crossed the border.
core.cn: 在某地出生、长成，根从未越过边界。

branches.en: PEOPLE: the original inhabitants and a person born in the region.
branches.cn: 人：原初居民与在此地出生的人。

branches.en: NATURE: species and materials formed in this ground.
branches.cn: 自然：在这片土地上演化或形成的物种与材料。

branches.en: CULTURE: customs and languages shaped locally.
branches.cn: 文化：在当地成形的风俗与语言。

branches.en: DEVELOPMENT: growth from local resources and initiative.
branches.cn: 发展：由本地资源与主动性产生的成长。

branches.en: CONTRAST: what belongs here against what was imported.
branches.cn: 对照：属于此地之物与输入之物。

intro.en: Indigenous is indu- plus gignere plus -ous. The items below show the birth family and the forms built directly on this adjective.
intro.cn: indigenous 是 indu- 加 gignere 再加 -ous。下列条目展示“出生”词族，以及直接建立在这个形容词上的形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the native noun, the begetting verb and the archaic prefix. Together they spell out 'born inside'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出本地人名词、生育动词与古体前缀。三者合起来拼出“生于其内”。

items.example: The olive is indigenous to the region.

items.exampleCN: 最先征询的是本地居民。

items.example: The court debated the meaning of indigeneity.
items.exampleCN: 法庭辩论了原住性的含义。
这一作物是本地培育的。

items.example: Indigenization of the syllabus took years.
items.exampleCN: 教学大纲的本土化花了多年。

items.example: They questioned the indigenousness of the breed.
items.exampleCN: 他们质疑这一品种的原生性。

items.structure: Latin nativus, from nasci 'to be born'
items.example: She is a native speaker of the language.
items.exampleCN: 她是这门语言的母语者。

definition_zh: 间接的；迂回的；不直截了当的
definition_en: not going straight from one point to another, or not stated openly
core_image: 一条绕过小山的路，虽远却通向同一座村庄
scene: 想问别人的年龄，直接问不太礼貌，只好绕着说。The flight is indirect and takes two days.
sceneCN: 这里 indirect 是「不直飞的」（第 1 个义项：路线不直）；句意是这趟航班要中转，走两天。

pos.zh: 形容词：间接的；迂回的；不直截了当的

derivatives.zh: 义为「间接地」，由本词加 -ly 构成
义为「直接的」，去掉 in- 即成肯定形式
义为「方向」，与本词同根
义为「主管、导演」，同根

senses.title: Not straight in route
senses.definition: not going straight, but by a longer way
senses.definitionCN: 不取直路，而是绕更远的路
senses.example: The flight is indirect and takes two days.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟航班要中转，走两天。
senses.why: The Latin regere means to rule or guide straight, and in- removes the straightness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 regere 意为「指引成直线」，in- 则取消了这份笔直。

senses.title: Not said or done openly
senses.titleCN: 不直说：含蓄或迂回的表达
senses.definition: not expressed in plain words, so that a listener must infer it
senses.definitionCN: 不用直白的话表达，听者须自行体会
senses.example: She made an indirect suggestion about leaving early.
senses.exampleCN: 她含蓄地提了一句早点走。
senses.why: A bend in the road becomes a bend in speech, used when plainness would be rude.
senses.whyCN: 道路的弯折变成话语的弯折，在直说会失礼时使用。

senses.title: As a secondary effect
senses.definition: happening as a result of something else rather than immediately
senses.definitionCN: 作为他事的结果而发生，而非直接产生
senses.example: The new road had indirect effects on local shops.
senses.exampleCN: 新路对本地商店产生了间接影响。
senses.why: Causes can work through a middle object, and the word marks that missing link.
senses.whyCN: 原因可以经由一个中间环节起作用，这个词就标出这条隐藏的链。

senses.title: Of light or cost, reflected
senses.titleCN: 间接的：光线或费用经反射、转嫁
senses.definition: of light, coming from a surface rather than the source; of costs, paid other than by direct charges
senses.definitionCN: 光线经表面反射而来；费用不经直接收取而是转嫁
senses.example: Soft indirect lighting makes the room feel bigger.
senses.exampleCN: 柔和的间接照明让房间显得更大。
senses.why: The same bend applies to physics and to money: the light and the cost both arrive by a detour.
senses.whyCN: 同一道弯折也适用于物理与金钱：光和钱都是绕道而来的。

senses.title: In grammar, reported speech
senses.titleCN: 间接引语：语法上的转述
senses.definition: used in grammar of speech reported without quotation marks
senses.definitionCN: 语法上指不用引号转述他人话语
senses.example: Change the sentence into indirect speech.
senses.exampleCN: 把这句话改成间接引语。
senses.why: Reported speech is one step away from the original voice, another detour.
senses.whyCN: 转述离原声已隔了一层，又是一次绕道。

intro.en: Indirect is in-, not, plus direct, from Latin dirigere, to set straight.
intro.cn: indirect 是 in-（不）加 direct，后者源自拉丁语 dirigere「使之笔直」。

items.en: Dirigere meant to set in line or to guide.
items.cn: dirigere 意为排成直线或引导。

items.en: Indirectus meant winding, not straight.
items.cn: indirectus 意为弯曲的、不直的。

items.en: English used indirect for crooked paths and for devious behaviour.
items.cn: 英语用 indirect 形容弯曲的路与不坦荡的行为。

items.en: Grammar adopted it for reported speech in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 语法学在十八世纪用它指转述话语。

items.en: Economics and lighting added the senses of shifted cost and reflected light.
items.cn: 经济学与照明又添上转嫁费用与反射光线之义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the direct root; the near-meaning group holds words for winding or roundabout.
note.cn: 形近组共用 direct 词根；近义组收表示迂回绕行的词。

entries.definition: Going straight or said plainly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「直接的」，去掉 in- 即成。

entries.definition: In a roundabout way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「间接地」。

entries.definition: The way something goes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「方向」，同根。

entries.definition: Long and not direct.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「绕路的、迂回的」。

entries.definition: Bending repeatedly along its length.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「蜿蜒的」。

entries.definition: Understood without being said.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「暗示的、含蓄的」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the road around the hill, the plain-speaking contrast and the grammar term.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借绕山的路、与直言相对的写法以及语法术语。

normal.en: In plus direct: the line is bent, but the destination may still be reached.
normal.cn: in 加 direct：直线被折弯，终点却仍能到。

normal.en: Direct speech quotes; indirect speech reports: one small word changes the whole grammar of a story.
normal.cn: 直接引语加引号，间接引语转述：一个小前缀改了整个句子的语法。

normal.en: An indirect route is often cheaper than a direct flight, the bend has a price.
normal.cn: 迂回航线常比直飞便宜，弯折自有其代价。

normal.en: Indirect lighting means the bulb faces a wall, and the wall does the shining.
normal.cn: 间接照明是灯泡对着墙，由墙来发光。

normal.en: Being indirect in speech is not lying, only asking the listener to walk one extra step.
normal.cn: 说话迂回不是撒谎，只是让听者多走一步。

abstract.en: Every direct line is a decision to ignore the landscape.
abstract.cn: 每条直线都是一项不顾地形的决定。

abstract.en: Indirection is how fragile systems survive shocks, by travelling around them.
abstract.cn: 迂回是脆弱系统躲过冲击的方式：绕过去。

abstract.en: Not saying a thing plainly is still a way of saying it.
abstract.cn: 不把话说直白，也仍然是在说。

examples.en: They took an indirect route through the mountains.
examples.cn: 他们走了一条翻山的迂回路线。

examples.en: The cause of the illness was indirect.
examples.cn: 病因是间接的。

examples.en: He gave an indirect answer to my question.
examples.cn: 他对我的问题含糊其辞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印地瑞克特」——印刷地图上标的路绕了一大圈，是间接的。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ dirigere（使之笔直，源自 regere「引导」）→ indirectus；同根词有 direct、direction、director、erect。

sensesIntro.en: Indirect denies a straight line, and the bent line reappears in routes, in speech, in causes, in light and money, and finally in grammar.
sensesIntro.cn: indirect 否定一条直线，而这条被折弯的线又在路线、话语、因果、光线与开销，最后在语法中复现。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road bending around a hill yet still reaching the village.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条绕过小山的路，最终仍到村庄。

branches.en: ROUTE LINE: the journey takes a longer way.
branches.cn: 路线线：行程绕了更远的路。

branches.en: SPEECH LINE: the meaning travels around the words.
branches.cn: 话语线：意思绕开了字面。

branches.en: CAUSAL LINE: effect arrives through a middle thing.
branches.cn: 因果线：效果经由中间环节到达。

branches.en: PHYSICAL LINE: light and cost arrive from a surface.
branches.cn: 物理线：光与费用从表面传来。

branches.en: GRAMMAR LINE: the voice of another is passed on.
branches.cn: 语法线：把别人的话转述出去。

intro.en: A negative prefix on a root meaning to guide straight, with a participial adjective ending.
intro.cn: 一个否定前缀加在意为「引导成直线」的词根上，再接分词形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin in-, not, plus dirigere, to set straight, plus -ectus gave indirectus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in-「不」加 dirigere「使之笔直」加 -ectus，构成 indirectus。

definition_zh: 必不可少的；不可或缺的
definition_en: so important that it cannot be done without
core_image: 一栋房子没了承重的那根柱，整片屋顶都会塌下来
scene: 收拾行李时，总有几样东西放不下也带不走。A good dictionary is indispensable for a translator.
sceneCN: 这里 indispensable 是「不可或缺的」（第 1 个义项：少了就不行）；句意是译者的好词典是少不了的。

pos.zh: 形容词：必不可少的；不可或缺的

collocations.phrase: an indispensable member of the team
collocations.zh: 团队中不可缺少的一员

derivatives.zh: 义为「可省去的」，去掉 in- 即成反义
义为「分发、配药」，是本词的动词根
义为「必不可少地」

senses.title: Cannot be done without
senses.titleCN: 不可少：少了就无法完成
senses.definition: too necessary to be given up or left out
senses.definitionCN: 太必要，以致不能舍弃或省略
senses.example: A good dictionary is indispensable for a translator.
senses.exampleCN: 对译者来说，一部好词典是少不了的。
senses.why: Latin dispensare means to weigh out and distribute, and in- with -able says this cannot be excused from the count.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 dispensare 意为「称量分发」，in- 加 -able 表示这种东西不能从账上免掉。

senses.title: Of a person, no substitute available
senses.titleCN: 无可替代：指某人无可取代
senses.definition: describing a person whose role nobody else can fill
senses.definitionCN: 形容某人的角色无人能替
senses.example: She is indispensable to the small clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 对这家小诊所来说，她是不可或缺的。
senses.why: A role, like a supply, can run out: without this person the work stops.
senses.whyCN: 角色也像物资，会断供：没有这个人，工作就停。

senses.title: Of an object, part of routine life
senses.titleCN: 日用必需：已成生活惯例
senses.definition: of a thing, so woven into daily habit that its absence is felt at once
senses.definitionCN: 指某物已融入日常习惯，一缺立刻被察觉
senses.example: The phone has become indispensable in daily life.
senses.exampleCN: 手机在日常生活中已变得不可或缺。
senses.why: Habit makes things necessary even when nothing forces us to keep them.
senses.whyCN: 习惯让东西变得必要，哪怕没有外力逼我们留着。

senses.title: In philosophy, absolutely necessary
senses.titleCN: 哲理用法：绝对必需之物
senses.definition: in abstract argument, something whose absence would make the whole system fail
senses.definitionCN: 在抽象论证中，指缺失会使整个体系崩塌的东西
senses.example: Trust is indispensable to any lasting agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 对任何持久的约定来说，信任都是不可或缺的。
senses.why: The word rises from goods to ideas: what cannot be dispensed with in logic is just as concrete.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从货物升到观念：逻辑上省不掉的东西，同样具体。

intro.en: Indispensable is in-, not, plus dispensable, from Latin dispensare, to weigh out and share.
intro.cn: indispensable 是 in-（不）加 dispensable，后者源自拉丁语 dispensare「称量分发」。

items.en: Pendere meant to hang, and so to weigh.
items.cn: pendere 意为「悬挂」，进而指「称重」。

items.en: Dispensare meant to weigh out and hand out shares.
items.cn: dispensare 意为称量后分发各份。

items.en: Dispensare also meant to grant exemption from a rule.
items.cn: dispensare 又指免除某项规矩。

items.en: Indispensable appeared for duties that could not be excused.
items.cn: indispensable 起初用于不能免除的义务。

items.en: The word widened to mean anything no plan can go without.
items.cn: 后来词义扩大，指任何计划都省不掉的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -pens- weighing root; the near-meaning group holds words for necessity.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -pens-「称量」词根；近义组收表示必要性的词。

entries.definition: That can be done without.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可省去的」，与本词相反。

entries.definition: To give out or to do without.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「分发」或「免除」。

entries.definition: Money paid out.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「花费」，同根。

entries.definition: Absolutely necessary.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「必需的」，语气最重。

entries.definition: Necessary for life or success.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「至关重要的」。

entries.definition: Decisive for the outcome.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「关键的」，重在决定结果。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the load-bearing column and the account from which nothing can be excused.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借房子的承重柱，以及一笔什么也免不掉的账。

normal.en: In plus dispensable: cannot be dispensed with, cannot be struck off the list.
normal.cn: in 加 dispensable：省不掉，也划不掉。

normal.en: Imagine a table missing one leg: the missing leg was indispensable.
normal.cn: 想一张少了一条腿的桌子：缺的那条正是不可缺的。

normal.en: The -able says it can be dispensed with; the in- says no, not this one.
normal.cn: -able 说「可以省」，in- 说：这一个不行。

normal.en: A pharmacist dispenses medicine; what cannot be dispensed is indispensable.
normal.cn: 药剂师 dispense 药；不能 dispense 掉的，就是 indispensable。

normal.en: Used of people, the word is a compliment, but also a warning about workload.
normal.cn: 用在人身上，这是夸奖，也是关于工作量的警告。

abstract.en: What is indispensable is defined by a counterfactual: the plan fails without it.
abstract.cn: 「不可或缺」由反事实定义：没有它，计划就失败。

abstract.en: Necessity is often manufactured by habit rather than by nature.
abstract.cn: 必要性常由习惯制造，而非由天性规定。

abstract.en: Every system hides one part it could never replace, and that part holds it up.
abstract.cn: 每个系统都藏着一个再也换不掉的部件，而正是它把系统撑住。

examples.en: Clean water is indispensable to public health.
examples.cn: 清洁的水对公共卫生不可或缺。

examples.en: He soon made himself indispensable at the office.
examples.cn: 他很快成了办公室里离不开的人。

examples.en: Bicycles are indispensable in this flat town.
examples.cn: 在这座平坦的小城里，自行车必不可少。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬地斯彭瑟伯」——硬地上的那台喷雾器是干活必不可少的。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ dispensare（称量分发、免除），源出 pendere（悬挂、称重）；同根词 dispense、dispensable、expense、pendant。

sensesIntro.en: Indispensable says that one item cannot be taken off the list: it holds for tools, for people, for habits and for ideas.
sensesIntro.cn: indispensable 说的是某样东西不能从清单上划掉：工具如此，人、习惯与观念也如此。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a load-bearing column without which the roof falls.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根抽掉屋顶就塌的承重柱。

branches.en: TOOL LINE: an object the work cannot start without.
branches.cn: 工具线：没它工作就开不了。

branches.en: PERSON LINE: a role nobody else can fill.
branches.cn: 人物线：一个没人能补上的角色。

branches.en: HABIT LINE: a thing whose absence is felt at once.
branches.cn: 习惯线：一缺就立刻被察觉的东西。

branches.en: THEORY LINE: a condition the whole system rests on.
branches.cn: 理论线：整个体系所依赖的条件。

branches.en: VALUE LINE: praise for a person, warning for a team.
branches.cn: 价值线：对人人是赞美，对团队是警示。

intro.en: A negative prefix stacked on a weighing root, with an ability ending on top.
intro.cn: 否定前缀叠在「称量」词根上，最外层再接表能力的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- plus dispensare plus -abilis built indispensable in French and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in- 加 dispensare 加 -abilis，经法语进入英语，成为 indispensable。

latinEntries.meaning: that can be given out or excused

definition_zh: 个人；个体；单独的；独特的
definition_en: a single person, or belonging to one person only and not shared
core_image: 一整块面团被切开，每一小块都还完整地存在
scene: 班上四十个人，每个人都不一样。Each individual has different needs.
sceneCN: 这里 individual 是「个人、个体」（第 1 个义项：单个的人）；句意是每个人都有不同的需求。

pos.zh: 名词：个人；个体
形容词：个别的；单独的；独特的

derivatives.zh: 义为「个性、个体性」，由本词加 -ity 构成
义为「个人主义」
义为「分别地、逐个地」
义为「分开」，是本词的核心词根

senses.title: A single human being
senses.definition: one person, thought of separately from the group
senses.definitionCN: 一个人，与群体分开来考虑
senses.example: Each individual has different needs.
senses.exampleCN: 每个人都有不同的需求。
senses.why: Latin dividere means to split, and in- denies it: an individual is a person who cannot be split further.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 dividere 意为「分割」，in- 加以否定：individual 就是无法再被分割的一个人。

senses.title: One apart from the rest
senses.titleCN: 单独的：与其余分开的一份
senses.definition: considered one by one rather than as a mass
senses.definitionCN: 逐个考虑而非作为整体
senses.example: The teacher gave individual help to weaker students.
senses.exampleCN: 老师给较弱的学生单独的帮助。
senses.why: To treat people individually is to refuse to lump them together.
senses.whyCN: 单独对待人，就是拒绝把人混成一堆。

senses.title: Belonging to one person only
senses.definition: owned or used by one person rather than shared
senses.definitionCN: 由一人拥有或使用，而非共用
senses.example: Each student has an individual desk.
senses.exampleCN: 每个学生有一张自己的桌子。
senses.why: What is not divided among people stays whole with one owner.
senses.whyCN: 不与人分的东西，完整地留在一个人手里。

senses.title: Markedly personal in style
senses.titleCN: 独特的：风格带个人印记
senses.definition: showing the particular character of one person
senses.definitionCN: 显示出某一个人的特殊性格
senses.example: Her paintings have a very individual style.
senses.exampleCN: 她的画有非常独特的风格。
senses.why: If a thing cannot be divided from its maker, it carries the maker's mark.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西若无法与创作者分开，就带着创作者的印记。

senses.title: In biology, a single organism
senses.definition: in biology, one living organism considered by itself
senses.definitionCN: 生物学上单独考虑的一个活体
senses.example: Scientists tracked the movements of each individual.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家追踪了每一个个体的活动。
senses.why: Ecology counts creatures one at a time, so it borrows the same unsplittable word.
senses.whyCN: 生态学一个个地数生物，于是也借了这个「不可再分」的词。

intro.en: Individual is Latin in-, not, plus dividere, to divide, plus -uus, so it means what cannot be divided.
intro.cn: individual 由拉丁语 in-（不）加 dividere（分割）加 -uus 构成，意为「不可再分的」。

items.en: Dividere meant to force apart or to split.
items.cn: dividere 意为强行分开、劈开。

items.en: Individuum was used for an atom or for a single thing.
items.cn: individuum 用来指原子或单一事物。

items.en: Scholars borrowed individuall for what exists as one whole.
items.cn: 学者借入 individuall，指作为整体存在的东西。

items.en: Philosophers used it for a single person or thing.
items.cn: 哲学家用它指单独的人或物。

items.en: Democratic debate made it a key word for personal rights.
items.cn: 关于民主的讨论让它成为个人权利的关键词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the divide root; the near-meaning group holds words for single units.
note.cn: 形近组共用 divide 词根；近义组收表示单一单位的词。

entries.definition: One by one, separately.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「分别地、逐个地」。

entries.definition: To separate into parts.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「分开」，本词词根。

entries.definition: The quality of being one distinct person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「个性、个体性」。

entries.definition: A human being.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「人」，最中性的说法。

entries.definition: One and no more.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「单一的」，重在数量。

entries.definition: Clearly different from others.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「与众不同的、独特的」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the uncut lump of dough and the in- that forbids cutting.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借那块没被切开的团子，以及禁止切割的 in-。

normal.en: In plus dividere: that which cannot be divided, and so one whole person.
normal.cn: in 加 dividere：切不开的东西，于是成为完整的一个「人」。

normal.en: Divide the class and you get individuals; the word is the shadow of the verb.
normal.cn: 把班级分开，得到一个个个人；这个词就是那个动词的影子。

normal.en: An individual desk is a desk you do not share.
normal.cn: individual desk 是一张你不与人共用的桌子。

normal.en: Individuality is what is left when the word is made a noun.
normal.cn: 加了 -ity，剩下的是 individuality，也就是个性。

normal.en: In biology every individual is counted separately, one at a time.
normal.cn: 在生物学里，每个个体都逐个计数。

abstract.en: A society is made of individuals, yet each one is more than a unit of the sum.
abstract.cn: 社会由个人组成，可每个个人都多于总和中的一个单位。

abstract.en: To be indivisible is not to be isolated; it is to be the smallest whole.
abstract.cn: 不可分不等于孤立，而是「最小的整体」。

abstract.en: The word reminds us that counting people is a choice, not a fact of nature.
abstract.cn: 这个词提醒我们：把人计数是一种选择，而非天然事实。

examples.en: Each individual is responsible for his own choices.
examples.cn: 每个人都要为自己的选择负责。

examples.en: The school offers individual lessons in music.
examples.cn: 学校开设一对一的音乐课。

examples.en: He writes in a highly individual way.
examples.cn: 他的写作风格极为独特。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因第维丢尔」——因为排第一的那个个体被单独留了下来。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ dividere（分割）+ -uus → individuus（不可分的）；同根词 divide、division、individuality、individualism。

sensesIntro.en: Individual starts from what cannot be cut and becomes a name for one person, for one's own things, for one's own style and for one organism in a field.
sensesIntro.cn: individual 从「切不开」出发，成为一个人、一个人的东西、一个人的风格，以及田野中的一个个体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: dough cut into pieces, each piece still whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：面团被切成块，每一块仍各自完整。

branches.en: PERSON LINE: a single human counted apart from the group.
branches.cn: 人身线：从群体中单独计数的人。

branches.en: COUNT LINE: help or attention given one at a time.
branches.cn: 计数线：逐个给出的帮助与关注。

branches.en: OWNERSHIP LINE: a thing not shared with anyone.
branches.cn: 归属线：不与任何人共用的东西。

branches.en: STYLE LINE: the maker's mark left on the work.
branches.cn: 风格线：创作者留在作品上的印记。

branches.en: BIOLOGY LINE: one organism in a population.
branches.cn: 生物线：种群中的一个个体。

intro.en: A negative prefix over a dividing root, with an adjective ending that makes it a thing.
intro.cn: 否定前缀压在「分割」词根上，再接形容词词尾把它变成一个「东西」。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- plus dividere plus -uus made individuus, then English individual.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in- 加 dividere 加 -uus 构成 individuus，英语再变为 individual。

items.meaning: the state of being one distinct self

latinEntries.meaningCN: 一个不可再分的单一体

definition_zh: 诱导；劝使；引起；导致；归纳；感应
definition_en: to persuade someone to do something, to cause something to happen, or to produce an effect by influence rather than direct force
core_image: 在前面引路的手：不推你，只在前面招手，让你自己走过去
scene: 这里指「诱导」。 The doctor explains that the drug may induce drowsiness, so the patient should not drive after taking it.
sceneCN: 这里 induce 是「引起、导致」（第 3 个义项：使某种状态发生）；句意：医生说这种药可能引起困倦，因此病人服药后不应开车。图中可辨识物件：药瓶、说明书、方向盘、打哈欠的病人。

senses.title: Lead by persuasion
senses.titleCN: 劝使：用说服把人引过去
senses.definition: to persuade or influence someone to do something, especially something they might not choose on their own
senses.definitionCN: 说服或影响某人做某事，尤指其原本未必会做的选择
senses.example: Nothing could induce him to leave the house before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 什么也无法劝使他在中午前离开家。
senses.why: Latin inducere is in- 'into' + ducere 'to lead'. The image is a guide walking ahead, not a hand pushing from behind; the person follows because the way has been made attractive.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 inducere 是 in-“进入”+ ducere“引导”。意象是在前面带路的人，而不是从背后推的手；人之所以跟随，是因为这条路被说得有吸引力。

senses.title: Bring about a physical reaction
senses.definition: to cause a physical response such as vomiting, sleep, or pain
senses.definitionCN: 引起呕吐、睡眠或疼痛等生理反应
senses.example: The syrup is used to induce vomiting after poisoning.
senses.exampleCN: 这种糖浆用于中毒后催吐。
senses.why: Medicine took the 'bring about' sense early: the drug does not persuade the body, it leads a reaction into existence.
senses.whyCN: 医学很早就采用了“使发生”这一义：药物并不说服身体，而是把一种反应引导出来、使其出现。

senses.title: Cause a state or condition
senses.definition: to cause a situation, feeling, or condition to begin to exist
senses.definitionCN: 使某种情况、感受或状态开始存在
senses.example: Uncertainty can induce stress in even experienced workers.
senses.exampleCN: 不确定性会给即使经验丰富的员工也带来压力。
senses.why: Once 'lead in' is extended from people to events, the object becomes a state: the cause leads the effect into being.
senses.whyCN: 当“引入”从人扩展到事件，宾语就变成一种状态：原因把结果引导出来、使之存在。

senses.title: Start labour medically
senses.titleCN: 引产：用医学手段启动分娩
senses.definition: to start the process of childbirth by medical means
senses.definitionCN: 用医学手段启动分娩过程
senses.example: The baby was induced two weeks early because of the risk.
senses.exampleCN: 由于存在风险，婴儿提前两周被引产。
senses.why: Here the body's own process is led into starting. The doctor does not force the birth directly but triggers the mechanism that produces it.
senses.whyCN: 这里是让身体自身的过程被“引入”启动。医生并不直接强行分娩，而是触发那个会产生分娩的机制。

senses.title: Derive a general rule from particular cases
senses.definition: to reach a general principle by reasoning from specific observations
senses.definitionCN: 从具体观察出发，通过推理得到一般原理
senses.example: From these samples we can induce a general law of growth.
senses.exampleCN: 从这些样本中，我们可以归纳出一条普遍的生长规律。
senses.why: The 1560s logic sense treats reasoning as a path: individual cases are led into a general conclusion. This is induction, the mirror image of deduction.
senses.whyCN: 16 世纪 60 年代产生的逻辑义把推理看成一条路：个别事例被引导到一个一般结论。这就是归纳，与演绎正好相反。

senses.title: Produce a current by electromagnetic induction
senses.titleCN: 电磁感应：产生感应电流
senses.definition: to produce an electric current or voltage in a conductor by changing a magnetic field
senses.definitionCN: 通过改变磁场，在导体中产生电流或电压
senses.example: A changing magnetic field induces a current in the coil.
senses.exampleCN: 变化的磁场会在线圈中产生感应电流。
senses.why: The 1777 electrical sense keeps the same structure: no direct push, only influence at a distance, and the current is 'led into' the wire.
senses.whyCN: 1777 年出现的电学义保持同一结构：没有直接推力，只有隔空的影响，电流被“引入”导线。

senses.title: Give an object an induced charge or magnetism
senses.titleCN: 使物体产生感应电荷或磁性
senses.definition: to give a material a charge, magnetization, or polarization through the influence of a nearby field
senses.definitionCN: 借附近场的影响，使材料带上电荷、磁性或极化
senses.example: The rod induces a positive charge on the near side of the sphere.
senses.exampleCN: 这根棒使球体靠近的一侧产生正电荷。
senses.why: Induction is influence without contact. One body's field leads charges or domains in another body to rearrange, so the effect appears without being carried in.
senses.whyCN: 感应是不接触的影响。一个物体的场引导另一个物体中的电荷或磁畴重新排列，因此效应出现却没有被直接搬运进去。

senses.title: Bring a biological state into being
senses.titleCN: 诱导生物状态：分化或表达
senses.definition: in biology, to cause cells, genes, or organisms to enter a particular state
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中，使细胞、基因或生物体进入某种特定状态
senses.example: The protein induces the stem cells to become nerve cells.
senses.exampleCN: 这种蛋白质诱导干细胞变成神经细胞。
senses.why: Developmental biology borrows the causative sense again: a signal leads a cell down one path rather than pushing it there.
senses.whyCN: 发育生物学再次借用“使发生”义：信号把细胞引向某条路径，而不是把它推过去。

senses.title: Lead in; introduce (archaic literal sense)
senses.definition: in older usage, to lead or bring someone into a place, state, or office
senses.definitionCN: 较旧用法中，把某人引入某地、某种状态或职位
senses.example: The rite was said to induce the novice into the order.
senses.exampleCN: 据说那仪式会把新人引入该修道会。
senses.why: This is the Latin sense almost unchanged. Modern English usually replaced it with introduce or induct, but it explains why every other sense contains 'lead into'.
senses.whyCN: 这几乎是未变的拉丁本义。现代英语通常用 introduce 或 induct 取代它，但它解释了为什么其他每个义项都含“引入”这一成分。

intro.en: Induce comes from Latin inducere 'to lead into'. Its history is a single image carried across persuasion, medicine, logic and electricity. The critical root contrast is ducere 'lead' versus dicare 'proclaim' and dividere 'divide'.
intro.cn: induce 来自拉丁语 inducere“引入、引导”。它的历史是同一个意象被带到说服、医学、逻辑与电学中。关键要区分 ducere“引导”、dicare“宣告”与 dividere“分开”。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'to lead by persuasions or inducements'. The subject leads another person's will, not their body.
items.cn: 最早在英语中记录为“用说服或诱因引导”。动作的主体引导的是他人的意愿，而不是他人的身体。

items.en: The sense 'to bring about, cause' appears, first in medical writing and then in general use. From here come induce sleep and induce vomiting.
items.cn: “使发生、引起”的义项出现，先用于医学写作，再进入一般用法。induce sleep 与 induce vomiting 都由此而来。

items.en: Inducere is in- 'into' + ducere 'to lead, draw'. Ducere is about guiding a path; dicare (in indicate) is about proclaiming; dividere (in individual) is about splitting. Imply uses plicare 'fold', impose uses ponere 'place', implement uses plere 'fill'.
items.cn: inducere 是 in-“进入”+ ducere“引导、牵引”。ducere 关乎带路；indicate 中的 dicare 关乎宣告；individual 中的 dividere 关乎分开。imply 用 plicare“折”，impose 用 ponere“放”，implement 用 plere“填满”。

items.en: The logical sense 'to infer by reasoning' is recorded, together with induction: particulars lead the mind to a general rule.
items.cn: 逻辑义“通过推理得出”有记录，同时出现 induction：个别事例把心灵引向一般规律。

items.en: The electrical sense appears: a changing magnetic field induces a current. Faraday's law of 1831 later gave the effect its exact form, but the verb came first.
items.cn: 电学义出现：变化的磁场会感应出电流。1831 年法拉第定律后来给出这一效应的精确形式，但动词用法在先。

items.en: Medicine induces labour and biology induces differentiation or gene expression. Inducer and inducible become standard technical terms.
items.cn: 医学上用 induce labour（引产），生物学上用 induce 表示诱导分化或基因表达。inducer 与 inducible 成为标准术语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the duc- root; the near-meaning group separates persuasion, causation and generation.
note.cn: 形近组共享 duc- 词根；近义组区分“劝”“致”“生”。

entries.definition: to install someone formally in an office or group. It is the concrete 'lead in' sense that induce has mostly lost.
entries.definitionCN: 正式使某人就职或加入某团体。它是 induce 已大体失去的“引入”本义的具体版本。

entries.definition: the act of inducting; reasoning from particulars to a rule; or the production of current by a changing field.
entries.definitionCN: 就职；归纳推理；或由变化磁场产生电流。

entries.definition: something offered to persuade a person to act.
entries.definitionCN: 诱因；用来劝使某人行动的东西。

entries.definition: to make someone agree or decide by giving reasons. It stresses argument; induce stresses the attraction of the offered path.
entries.definitionCN: 通过给出理由使某人同意或决定。它强调论证；induce 强调所提供路径的吸引力。

entries.definition: to cause someone to do something, often suddenly. It stresses the spark rather than the guidance.
entries.definitionCN: 促使某人做某事，常指突然触发。它强调火花，而不是引导。

entries.definition: to make something happen. It is the neutral general word; induce often implies influence rather than direct force.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事发生。它中性而笼统；induce 常暗示影响而非直接施力。

entries.definition: to produce or create something, especially energy or a result. It stresses output, not the leading of a process.
entries.definitionCN: 产生或创造某物，尤指能量或结果。它强调产出，而不是对过程的引导。

normalIntro.en: Real roots and real phrases; the in- here means 'into', not 'not'.
normalIntro.cn: 真实词根与真实短语；这里的 in- 是“进入”，不是“不”。

normal.en: ducere 'lead': induce is to lead someone into doing something, not to push them.
normal.cn: ducere“引导”：induce 是把某人引向做某事，而不是推他。

normal.en: The in- of induce is 'into', unlike the negative in- of individual.
normal.cn: induce 的 in- 是“进入”，不同于 individual 的否定前缀 in-。

normal.en: Conduct, produce, reduce and deduce all contain ducere 'lead'; induce adds 'into'.
normal.cn: conduct、produce、reduce、deduce 都含 ducere“引导”；induce 只是加上“进入”。

normal.en: Induce vs indicate: dicare 'proclaim' points with the voice, ducere 'lead' walks ahead.
normal.cn: induce 与 indicate：dicare“宣告”用声音指向，ducere“引导”则在前面走。

normal.en: Induction climbs from cases to a rule; deduction walks back down from the rule.
normal.cn: induction 从个案爬上规则；deduction 从规则往下走。

abstract.en: Picture a shepherd walking ahead of the flock, never driving from behind.
abstract.cn: 想象一个牧人在羊群前面走，从不从后面驱赶。

abstract.en: Influence at a distance: the wire never touches the magnet, yet the current appears.
abstract.cn: 隔空的影响：导线从未碰到磁铁，电流却出现了。

abstract.en: A good teacher induces curiosity: nothing is pushed, something is led out.
abstract.cn: 好老师会诱导好奇心：没有东西被推，只有东西被引出来。

examples.en: The advertisement is designed to induce people to buy on impulse.
examples.cn: 这则广告旨在诱导人们冲动购买。

examples.en: Certain drugs can induce drowsiness within an hour.
examples.cn: 某些药物能在一小时内引起困倦。

examples.en: From these cases the researchers induced a general pattern.
examples.cn: 研究者从这些案例中归纳出一个普遍模式。

dict_mnemonic.text: “引道士”——请来一位道士，先在前头引路，再劝你跟他走，路上还施法引起变化 → induce 引导、劝使、引起

root: 源自拉丁语 inducere“引入、引导”，由 in-“进入”+ ducere“引导”构成，过去分词 inductus；核心是“在前面带路，而不是从后面推”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of induce, all built on 'lead into'. A person is led by persuasion, a body is led into a reaction, a mind is led to a rule, and a wire is led into carrying current.
sensesIntro.cn: induce 的九个义项都建立在“引入”上。人被说服引过去，身体被引向某种反应，心灵被引向一条规律，导线则被引到载流状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a guide walks ahead and the other person chooses to follow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个引路人在前面走，另一个人选择跟上。

branches.en: PERSUASION: the path is made attractive so that the will follows it.
branches.cn: 说服：路被说得有吸引力，意愿便跟着走。

branches.en: CAUSATION: a drug, a stressor or a doctor leads a physical process into starting.
branches.cn: 因果：药物、压力源或医生把一个生理过程引向启动。

branches.en: LOGIC: particular cases lead the mind to a general rule.
branches.cn: 逻辑：个别事例把心灵引向一般规律。

branches.en: PHYSICS: a field leads charges or current into motion without contact.
branches.cn: 物理：场在不接触的情况下把电荷或电流引向运动。

branches.en: STATE AND PLACE: a signal leads a cell into a state; an old rite leads a person into a group.
branches.cn: 状态与地点：信号把细胞引入某种状态；旧仪式把人引入某个团体。

intro.en: Induce is in- + duc- + -e. The -duce family is large: conduct, produce, reduce, deduce, introduce. English builds inducement, induction, inductive, inductor, inducible and inducer.
intro.cn: induce 是 in- + duc- + -e。-duce 词族很大：conduct、produce、reduce、deduce、introduce。英语另加 -ment、-ion、-ive、-or、-ible、-er 构成派生词。

latinIntro.en: Latin inducere 'lead in' and ducere 'lead'. Relatives include duct, duke, ductile and educate (ducere + ex- 'out').
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族是 inducere“引入”与 ducere“引导”。同族词包括 duct、duke、ductile、educate（ducere + ex-“出”）。

items.meaning: something that persuades a person to act
items.meaningCN: 诱因；劝使某人行动的事物
items.example: The company offered a bonus as an inducement.
items.exampleCN: 公司提供奖金作为诱因。

items.meaning: the act of inducting; reasoning from cases; magnetic or electric induction
items.meaningCN: 就职；归纳；磁感应或电感应
items.example: Induction begins with observed cases, not with a rule.
items.exampleCN: 归纳从观察到的个案开始，而不是从规则开始。

items.meaning: based on induction, or relating to electrical induction
items.meaningCN: 归纳的；归纳性的；电感的
items.example: The study uses inductive reasoning rather than a fixed model.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究使用归纳推理，而不是固定模型。

items.example: The theory was built inductively from field notes.
items.exampleCN: 这一理论是从田野笔记归纳建立起来的。

items.meaning: a component that stores energy in a magnetic field
items.example: The circuit needs a larger inductor to smooth the current.
items.exampleCN: 这个电路需要更大的电感器来平稳电流。

items.meaning: the property of a circuit that opposes changes in current
items.meaningCN: 电感；抵抗电流变化的性质
items.exampleCN: 电感以亨利为单位测量。

items.meaning: to lead in, persuade, or bring about
items.example: The signal induces the cell to divide.
items.exampleCN: 这一信号诱导细胞分裂。

items.meaning: able to be induced or activated
items.example: The gene is inducible by heat shock.
items.exampleCN: 这个基因可被热激诱导。

items.meaning: a substance or signal that induces a state
items.example: The sugar acts as an inducer of the enzyme.
items.exampleCN: 这种糖充当该酶的诱导物。

items.meaning: to bring a person or thing into a place or group
items.example: She introduced the new method to the team.
items.exampleCN: 她向团队介绍了这种新方法。

latinEntries.meaning: to lead in, bring in; to induce, persuade
a leading, drawing; the perfect participle 'led'
latinEntries.meaningCN: 引导；被引导的（ducere 的完成分词）

definition_zh: 归纳；归纳法；就职（入伍）典礼；感应；诱导
definition_en: reasoning from particular cases to a general rule, or the act of bringing someone or something into a role, a body or a state
core_image: 桌上排着一列深浅不同的样本，研究员从最浅的一支开始记录，最后在纸页顶端写下一条通则
scene: 实验室的桌上摆着一排颜色深浅不一的溶液，研究员从最浅的开始逐一记录，再把共同点写到本子上。Induction begins with many small observations and ends with one general rule.
sceneCN: 这里 induction 指「从许多个别事例推出通则」（第 1 个义项：归纳推理）；句意为归纳从许多细小的观察开始，最后得到一个通则。

使正式就职；征召入伍（同一拉丁分词的另一条进入路径）

senses.title: Reasoning from particular cases
senses.definition: the move from a number of observed instances to a general statement about all such cases
senses.definitionCN: 从若干被观察的实例走向关于所有同类情形的概括陈述
senses.example: Induction begins with many small observations and ends with one general rule.
senses.exampleCN: 归纳从许多细小的观察开始，最后得到一个通则。
senses.why: The Latin verb means 'to lead in', so the mind is led from scattered cases into one rule.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「领进来」，心智被从零散事例领进一条规则。

senses.title: The method itself
senses.definition: the systematic procedure of collecting cases and generalizing from them
senses.definitionCN: 收集事例并从中概括的系统程序
senses.example: Bacon urged induction as a corrective to inherited opinion.
senses.exampleCN: 培根主张以归纳法纠正沿袭的成见。
senses.why: A single move becomes a repeatable procedure with rules of its own.
senses.whyCN: 单次动作变成了有自身规则、可重复的程序。

senses.title: A ceremony of taking office
senses.definition: the formal occasion on which a person is installed in a position
senses.definitionCN: 正式使某人进入某个职位的场合
senses.example: The new rector's induction filled the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 新校长的就职典礼坐满了礼堂。
senses.why: The old sense of leading someone in survives socially: a person is led into a chair.
senses.whyCN: 「把某人领进来」的古义在社会场合留存：一个人被领进一个位子。

senses.title: Admission into an organization
senses.definition: the process of bringing a recruit or member formally into a group
senses.definitionCN: 正式把新成员引入某个群体的过程
senses.example: Induction into the unit took two weeks of training.
senses.exampleCN: 加入该部队的入门训练花了两周。
senses.why: Institutions literalize the image: a body is brought inside a gate and a set of rules.
senses.whyCN: 机构把这个意象字面化：一个人被带进一道门与一套规则之内。

senses.title: Electromagnetic induction
senses.definition: the production of a current in a conductor by a changing magnetic field
senses.definitionCN: 变化的磁场在导体中产生电流
senses.example: Faraday's induction made the electric motor possible.
senses.exampleCN: 法拉第的电磁感应使电动机成为可能。
senses.why: Nothing is physically led in; a state is induced in a nearby body without contact.
senses.whyCN: 并没有东西被实际领入；一种状态在不接触的情况下被引发于邻近物体。

senses.title: Induction of anaesthesia
senses.definition: the process of bringing a patient into anaesthesia
senses.definitionCN: 使病人进入麻醉状态的过程
senses.example: Induction takes about two minutes in adults.
senses.exampleCN: 成人的麻醉诱导约需两分钟。
senses.why: Medicine keeps the metaphor of leading a person into a state.
senses.whyCN: 医学保留了「把一个人领进某种状态」的比喻。

senses.title: Biological induction
senses.definition: the triggering of gene activity or tissue development by a signal
senses.definitionCN: 由信号触发基因活动或组织发育
senses.example: Induction of the gene followed the hormone signal.
senses.exampleCN: 该基因的诱导随激素信号而来。
senses.why: A signal from outside switches on a programme inside, which is the same leading-in at cellular scale.
senses.whyCN: 外部信号开启内部程序，这是细胞尺度上的同一种「引入」。

senses.title: The conclusion reached
senses.definition: the general statement produced by the procedure, viewed as its output
senses.definitionCN: 由该程序产生、被当作其产物的一般陈述
senses.example: The induction held until a single counter-example appeared.
senses.exampleCN: 这个归纳结论一直成立，直到出现一个反例。
senses.why: The movement of thought leaves a product behind, and the word can name that product too.
senses.whyCN: 思维的运动留下产物，这个词也能指那个产物。

intro.en: Induction comes from a Latin noun of action built on a verb meaning 'to lead in'. The logical sense grew out of the physical one.
intro.cn: induction 来自拉丁语的表动作名词，它建立在一个意为「领进来」的动词上。逻辑义是从物理义生长出来的。

items.en: Ducere meant 'to lead, draw, conduct'. It is one of the most productive verbs in the Latin vocabulary and supplies a large English family.
items.cn: ducere 意为「引领、拉、导」。它是拉丁语中构词能力最强的动词之一，提供了大批英语词。

items.en: The compound meant 'to lead or bring in', and also 'to introduce, to persuade'. The two shades have stayed together ever since.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为「引入、带进」，也指「介绍、劝说」。这两层意思此后一直并存。

items.en: The noun of action covered both a physical bringing in and, in later Latin, an argument that leads the mind to a conclusion.
items.cn: 这个表动作名词既涵盖物理上的引入，也在后来的拉丁语中指把心智引向结论的论证。

items.en: English took the noun in the fifteenth century; by the sixteenth it named the ceremony of installing a person in office.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪接受了这个名词；到 16 世纪它指使某人就职的典礼。

items.en: The method of generalizing from observed cases was promoted as a corrective to inherited reasoning, and the word became its standard name.
items.cn: 从观察事例概括的方法被提倡为对沿袭推理的纠正，这个词成了它的标准名称。

items.en: Nineteenth-century physics used the word for a current produced without contact, and medicine used it for bringing a patient into anaesthesia.
items.cn: 19 世纪的物理学用这个词指不接触而产生的电流，医学用同词指使病人进入麻醉。

note.en: The first group holds words built on the same leading-in verb that are constantly confused; the second holds near neighbours in reasoning.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「引入」动词、常被混淆的词；第二组是推理领域里的近义词。

entries.definition: Same Latin verb: to cause a state, to persuade, or to bring on labour; it is the everyday verb behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁动词：指使某种状态发生、劝说，或引产；是这个名词背后的日常动词。

entries.definition: Structurally the same verb but used for formal installation into a post, and for admission into military service.
entries.definitionCN: 结构上同源，但专用于正式使就职，以及征召入伍。

entries.definition: From the same leading verb with a prefix meaning 'down or away': it moves from general rules to particular cases.
entries.definitionCN: 同一「引领」动词加意为「向下、离开」的前缀：从通则走向个别情形。

entries.definition: The property of a circuit that opposes a change of current; it shares the electrical sense but names a measurement, not a process.
entries.definitionCN: 电路阻碍电流变化的性质；共享「电」这一义，但指一个量而非过程。

entries.definition: The broad statement produced by induction, stated as a result rather than as a method.
entries.definitionCN: 由归纳产生的宽泛陈述，被表述为结果而非方法。

entries.definition: Any move from evidence to conclusion, covering both the inductive and the deductive road.
entries.definitionCN: 从证据到结论的任何推进，涵盖归纳与演绎两条路。

entries.definition: It generalizes from samples to a quantity, where induction generalizes to a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 从样本概括到一个数量，而归纳概括到一条规则。

entries.definition: A transparent phrase for the ceremony sense, with no Latin root at all.
entries.definitionCN: 就职典礼义的大白话说法，完全不带拉丁词根。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin verb means 'lead in', so induction leads the mind from cases into a rule.
normal.cn: 拉丁动词意为「领进来」，所以归纳把心智从事例领进一条规则。

normal.en: The family runs induce, induct, induction, inductive, inductively.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 induce、induct、induction、inductive、inductively。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the domains: induction from examples, induction ceremony, electromagnetic induction.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：由例证归纳、就职典礼、电磁感应。

normal.en: The same leading verb, with a few other prefixes, gives conduct, produce, reduce and deduce.
normal.cn: 同一个「引领」动词配上别的前缀，就得到 conduct、produce、reduce、deduce。

normal.en: Philosophy knows it as the problem of induction: no number of cases can guarantee the rule.
normal.cn: 哲学把它称作归纳问题：再多事例也无法保证那条规则。

abstract.en: Picture a hand drawing one line through a hundred scattered dots.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在一百个散点上画出一条线。

abstract.en: Picture a door held open while someone is walked through it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门被扶着敞开，有人正被领过去。

abstract.en: Picture a magnet moving near a wire, and the wire answering without being touched.
abstract.cn: 想象一块磁铁在导线旁移动，导线没被碰却有了回应。

examples.en: Induction from a handful of cases is useful but never certain.
examples.cn: 从少数事例归纳有用，但从不保证确定。

examples.en: The induction of new staff includes a week of shadowing.
examples.cn: 新员工的入职引导包括一周的跟岗。

examples.en: The coil produces a current by induction when the field changes.
examples.cn: 磁场变化时，线圈通过感应产生电流。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（向内）+ duct（引导）＝ 把心智从一个个事例领进一条通则 → 归纳；也指把人领进职位或某种状态。

root: 拉丁 inductio「引入」，来自 inducere「领进来、引入」，由 in-「向内」+ ducere「引领」构成。同族有 induce、induct、deduce、conduct、produce、reduce。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one leading-in. The mind can be led from cases to a rule, the procedure can be made a method, a person can be led into an office or a unit, a state can be led into a body or a circuit, and the rule itself can be the thing left behind.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一次「领进来」展开。心智可以被从事例领进一条规则，程序可以被做成方法，一个人可以被领进职位或队伍，某种状态可以被引入身体或电路，而那条规则本身也可以是留下的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand leading someone through a doorway into a place they were not in before.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手领着某人穿过门口，进入他原本不在的地方。

branches.en: THE MOVE AND WHAT IT LEAVES: the leading-in of the mind, and the general statement that remains afterwards.
branches.cn: 这次引领与它留下的东西：把心智领进去，以及之后留下的那句概括。

branches.en: MADE INTO A PROCEDURE: one move repeated by rule becomes a method with a name.
branches.cn: 变成程序：一次动作按规则重复，就成了有名称的方法。

branches.en: PEOPLE LED THROUGH DOORS: into an office by ceremony, into a unit by training.
branches.cn: 被领过门的人：以典礼领进职位，以训练领进队伍。

branches.en: LED WITHOUT CONTACT: physics keeps only the effect, a state induced at a distance.
branches.cn: 不接触的引领：物理学只保留效果，即在远处被引发的状态。

branches.en: LED INTO A STATE: a patient into sleep, a cell into a switched-on programme.
branches.cn: 被领进某种状态：病人进入麻醉，细胞进入被开启的程序。

intro.en: Induction is a prefix plus a verb plus a noun ending, and each piece can be read separately.
intro.cn: induction 由前缀、动词与名词词尾构成，每一块都可以单独读出。

latinIntro.en: The leading verb with different prefixes builds a whole set of English verbs, so the family is unusually easy to read.
latinIntro.cn: 这个「引领」动词配上不同前缀，造出一整组英语动词，因此这个词族读起来格外容易。

items.example: The prefix marks movement toward an inside.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出朝内部去的运动。

items.structure: ducere, duxi, ductum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The root supplies the pulling hand.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供那只牵引的手。

items.example: The compound adds direction to the pulling.
items.exampleCN: 复合词在牵引之上加了方向。

items.example: The ending turns the verb into an event.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变成一个事件。

items.example: Induction led the mind from cases to a rule.
items.exampleCN: 归纳把心智从事例引向规则。

items.structure: induce (English verb from the Latin form)
items.example: The drug induces sleep within minutes.
items.exampleCN: 这种药几分钟内引起睡意。

items.structure: induct (English verb from the Latin participle)
items.example: They inducted her into the academy.
items.exampleCN: 他们正式接纳她进入学会。

items.example: An inductive step moves from cases to a rule.
items.exampleCN: 归纳的一步从事例走向规则。

items.example: The same verb with another prefix leads a group.
items.exampleCN: 同一动词配另一个前缀，就是引领一群人。

items.example: The prefix reverses the direction of travel.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把行进方向反过来。

derivatives.zh: 引起；诱导；劝说（拉丁动词「引入」进入英语，由「领进来」转为「使发生」）
使正式就职；征召入伍（同一拉丁分词的另一条进入路径）
归纳的；感应的（名词词干加形容词后缀）
以归纳方式（形容词加副词后缀）

definition_zh: 归纳的；由个别到一般的；感应的；诱导的
definition_en: relating to reasoning that moves from particular cases to a general rule, or to effects produced without direct contact
core_image: 七个样本按颜色排成一列，一条细线从最左端拉到最右端，线的另一端写着一条通则
scene: 地质课上，学生把七块岩石样本按颗粒大小排成一列，然后写下一条适用于整层的判断。Her inductive method turned seven samples into a single working rule.
sceneCN: 这里 inductive 指「由个别样本推向一般规则的」（第 2 个义项：由个别到一般）；句意为她的归纳方法把七块样本变成了一条可用的规则。

pos.zh: 归纳的；由个别到一般的；感应的；可被诱导的

collocations.zh: 归纳偏置（机器学习术语）

derivatives.zh: 归纳；感应（形容词背后的名词，指该过程或该现象）
以归纳方式（形容词加副词后缀）
归纳的性质（形容词加名词后缀）
电感器（拉丁动词加表器具的后缀，指利用感应的元件）

senses.title: Of inductive reasoning
senses.definition: belonging to the kind of inference that generalizes from observed cases
senses.definitionCN: 属于从被观察事例进行概括的那类推理
senses.example: Inductive reasoning cannot prove a rule, only support it.
senses.exampleCN: 归纳推理无法证明一条规则，只能支持它。
senses.why: The adjective simply labels the process named by the noun behind it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是给它背后那个名词所指的过程贴上标签。

senses.title: Proceeding from particulars to a general
senses.definition: describing a method that starts with individual facts and ends with a wider statement
senses.definitionCN: 形容从个别事实开始、以较宽陈述结束的方法
senses.example: Her inductive method turned seven samples into a single working rule.
senses.exampleCN: 她的归纳方法把七块样本变成了一条可用的规则。
senses.why: Direction is the whole point: the same facts read upward give a rule, read downward give instances.
senses.whyCN: 方向就是全部要点：同样的事实往上读得到规则，往下读得到实例。

senses.title: Of electrical induction
senses.definition: describing effects produced in a conductor by a changing magnetic field
senses.definitionCN: 形容由变化磁场在导体中产生的效应
senses.example: Inductive coupling charges the smaller coil without a wire.
senses.exampleCN: 电感耦合不用导线就给较小的线圈充电。
senses.why: Here nothing is led in physically; a state appears in a nearby body, which is the old image at a distance.
senses.whyCN: 这里没有东西被实际引入；一种状态出现在邻近物体上，这是那个古老意象的远距离版本。

senses.title: Of an inductor
senses.definition: in electronics, describing a component that stores energy in a magnetic field
senses.definitionCN: 在电子学中，形容以磁场储存能量的元件
senses.example: The inductive load made the switch arc.
senses.exampleCN: 电感负载使开关产生了电弧。
senses.why: A component is named for the effect it exploits, so the adjective attaches to hardware.
senses.whyCN: 元件因它所利用的效应而得名，于是这个形容词附着到硬件上。

senses.title: Capable of being induced
senses.definition: able to be brought about or brought on by an outside agent
senses.definitionCN: 能够被外部因素引起或触发的
senses.example: Some genes are inductive only under stress.
senses.exampleCN: 有些基因只在应激时才可被诱导。
senses.why: The passive possibility is expressed by the same ending that marks other capacities.
senses.whyCN: 被动的可能性由标记其他「能力」的同一词尾表达。

senses.title: Introductory or leading on
senses.definition: in older usage, describing remarks that lead the hearer into a subject
senses.definitionCN: 在较旧的用法中，形容把听者引入某个话题的开场话
senses.example: His inductive remarks prepared the audience for the argument.
senses.exampleCN: 他那段开场话为听众进入论证做了铺垫。
senses.why: The literal sense of leading someone in survives in this mild rhetorical use.
senses.whyCN: 「把某人领进来」的字面义在这种温和的修辞用法中留存。

senses.title: Empirical, based on observation
senses.definition: resting on what has been observed rather than on principles fixed in advance
senses.definitionCN: 依据已被观察到的内容，而非事先固定的原则
senses.example: The study took an inductive route, gathering cases before framing a theory.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究走归纳路线，先收集案例，再提出理论。
senses.why: When no framework is given, the only way forward is to look first and generalize later.
senses.whyCN: 在没有现成框架时，唯一的前进方式就是先看、后概括。

senses.title: A built-in assumption in learning systems
senses.definition: in machine learning, describing the assumptions a model makes in order to generalize from limited data
senses.definitionCN: 在机器学习中，形容模型为了从有限数据泛化而作出的假设
senses.example: Every model carries an inductive bias of some kind.
senses.exampleCN: 每个模型都带着某种归纳偏置。
senses.why: A machine that generalizes must be tilted toward some patterns, and the older word supplies the label.
senses.whyCN: 要泛化的机器必须偏向某些模式，这个古老的词为此提供了标签。

intro.en: Inductive is the adjective built on induction, with a Latin ending meaning 'having the nature of'. Its history is the history of the noun.
intro.cn: inductive 是建立在 induction 之上的形容词，带一个意为「具有……性质」的拉丁词尾。它的历史就是那个名词的历史。

items.en: The verb meant 'to lead'; the whole family is about direction of movement, literal or mental.
items.cn: 这个动词意为「引领」；整个词族都关乎运动的方向，无论是实际还是心智上的。

items.en: The compound meant 'to lead in', and its participle supplied the stem that English adjectives use.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为「引入」，它的分词提供了英语形容词所用的词干。

items.en: Late Latin formed an adjective on the participle, meaning 'of a bringing in'; it passed into the modern languages as a label for a kind of argument.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语在这个分词上造出形容词，意为「属于引入的」；它作为某类论证的标签传入近代语言。

items.en: English adopted the adjective in the sixteenth century, at first for rhetorical and then for logical use.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪接受了这个形容词，先用于修辞，后用于逻辑。

items.en: Physics gave the word its electrical sense, and engineering extended it to components that exploit the effect.
items.cn: 物理学给了它「电」这一义，工程学又把它扩展到利用该效应的元件上。

items.en: Learning theory and machine learning reused the word for the assumptions that allow generalization from limited data. Source uncertain: the deeper origin of the leading verb is not settled.
items.cn: 学习理论与机器学习再次使用这个词，指使有限数据得以泛化的那些假设。来源不确定：那个「引领」动词的更早来源没有定论。

note.en: The first group holds words that differ from inductive by a prefix or an ending; the second holds near neighbours in method.
note.cn: 第一组是与 inductive 只差一个前缀或词尾的词；第二组是方法上的近义词。

entries.definition: The same adjective pattern with a prefix meaning 'down from': it starts from general rules and works toward cases.
entries.definitionCN: 同样的形容词模式，前缀却意为「由……而下」：从通则出发走向个别情形。

entries.definition: The process or event itself; the adjective is used to modify a method, a step or a reasoning type.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程或事件本身；形容词用来修饰方法、步骤或推理类型。

entries.definition: The past participle: it says that something was brought about, not that a method generalizes.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词：说的是某事被引起，而不是某种方法在做概括。

entries.definition: A device, not a method; the ending marks a thing rather than a property.
entries.definitionCN: 指器件而非方法；词尾标记的是物，而不是性质。

entries.definition: It stresses reliance on observed data, which inductive methods usually need but do not define.
entries.definitionCN: 强调依赖观察数据；归纳方法通常需要它，但并不等于它。

entries.definition: A philosophical label for knowledge that comes after experience, wider than any one method.
entries.definitionCN: 哲学术语，指经验之后获得的知识，比任何一种方法都宽。

entries.definition: It describes work set up to produce observations, whereas inductive describes how conclusions are drawn from them.
entries.definitionCN: 形容为产生观察而安排的工作，而 inductive 形容如何从中得出结论。

entries.definition: It names a mathematical apparatus for generalizing from samples, one modern form of inductive work.
entries.definitionCN: 指从样本概括的一套数学工具，是归纳工作的现代形态之一。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means 'in' and the verb means 'lead': inductive work leads the mind inward from cases to a rule.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「向内」，动词意为「引领」：归纳工作把心智从事例领向一条规则。

normal.en: The family runs induce, induction, inductive, inductively, inductiveness, inductor.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 induce、induction、inductive、inductively、inductiveness、inductor。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: inductive reasoning, inductive method, inductive coupling.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：归纳推理、归纳方法、电感耦合。

normal.en: The opposite adjective is deductive, which travels the other way with the other prefix.
normal.cn: 反义的形容词是 deductive，用另一个前缀走相反方向。

normal.en: Machine learning speaks of an inductive bias, the tilt that lets a model generalize.
normal.cn: 机器学习讲「归纳偏置」，即让模型得以泛化的那种偏向。

abstract.en: Picture a rope pulled from many small pegs into one knot.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳从许多小木桩上收拢成一个结。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder whose rungs are separate facts.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子，每一级横档都是一个单独的事实。

abstract.en: Picture a magnet that makes a nearby needle turn before it is touched.
abstract.cn: 想象一块磁铁让旁边的针在被碰之前就转了方向。

examples.en: Inductive reasoning is powerful in discovery and weak in proof.
examples.cn: 归纳推理在发现上很有力，在证明上很弱。

examples.en: The team took an inductive approach, coding interviews before forming categories.
examples.cn: 团队采取归纳进路，先编码访谈，再形成类别。

examples.en: Inductive charging heats the phone less than a cable does.
examples.cn: 感应充电比线缆充电让手机发热更少。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（向内）+ duct（引领）+ ive（具有……性质的）＝ 把心智从个别事例领向通则的 → 归纳的。

root: 拉丁 inductivus「属于引入的」，来自 inducere「领进来」，由 in-「向内」+ ducere「引领」构成；更早来源不确定。同族有 induction、induce、deductive、inductor。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one adjective's reach. It can label a kind of inference, a direction of method, an electrical effect, a component, a capacity to be brought about, an introductory remark, an empirical stance, or an assumption built into a model.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个形容词的覆盖范围展开。它可以标记一类推理、一种方法的方向、一种电效应、一个元件、一种可被引起的性质、一段开场话、一种经验立场，或一个被装进模型里的假设。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line drawn from many separate dots up to a single knot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条线从许多分散的点拉向一个结。

chain: A TILT BUILT INTO THE MODEL

branches.en: THE LABEL AND THE DIRECTION: what kind of inference it is, and which way it travels.
branches.cn: 标签与方向：它是哪一类推理，以及它朝哪边行进。

branches.en: LOOK FIRST: when no framework exists, observation must come before the rule.
branches.cn: 先看：没有框架时，观察必须走在规则之前。

branches.en: ACROSS A GAP: the effect arrives without contact, and then the hardware is named for it.
branches.cn: 越过空隙：效应不接触就到达，随后硬件因它得名。

branches.en: BROUGHT ABOUT, OR LED IN: what can be caused, and the older habit of leading a listener in.
branches.cn: 被引起，或被领入：可被引起的东西，以及把听者领进来的旧习惯。

branches.en: THE MACHINE'S OWN TILT: generalization needs an assumption chosen in advance.
branches.cn: 机器自身的偏向：泛化需要一个事先选定的假设。

intro.en: Inductive is a Latin participle stem plus an adjective ending, so it is built from three recognisable pieces.
intro.cn: inductive 是拉丁分词词干加形容词词尾，因此由三块可辨认的成分构成。

latinIntro.en: The same leading verb underlies the noun and the verb, while the ending marks a property rather than an action.
latinIntro.cn: 同一个「引领」动词支撑着名词与动词，而词尾标记的是性质而非动作。

items.example: The prefix fixes the direction of the leading.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀固定了牵引的方向。

items.example: The root is the hand that pulls.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根就是那只拉的手。

items.example: The ending turns an action into a quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动作变成性质。

items.example: An inductive step goes from cases to a rule.
items.exampleCN: 归纳的一步从事例走向规则。

items.example: Induction is the process the adjective describes.
items.exampleCN: 归纳就是这个形容词所描述的过程。
这条规则是归纳得出的。

items.example: Researchers debated the inductiveness of the method.
items.exampleCN: 研究者争论这套方法有多强的归纳性。

items.example: The inductor stores energy in a magnetic field.
items.exampleCN: 电感器以磁场储存能量。

items.example: The two adjectives name opposite directions.
items.exampleCN: 这两个形容词命名相反的方向。

以归纳方式（形容词加副词后缀）
归纳的性质（形容词加名词后缀）
电感器（拉丁动词加表器具的后缀，指利用感应的元件）

definition_zh: 工业的；产业的；工业化的
definition_en: relating to industry, to factories and to the making of goods
core_image: 一排排厂房冒着白烟，机器在轰鸣
scene: 城市的边缘聚集着厂房与货仓。The old industrial area has been turned into a park.
sceneCN: 这里 industrial 是「工业的」（第 1 个义项：与工业和工厂有关）；句意是那片旧工业区已经被改成了公园。

pos.zh: 形容词：工业的；产业的；工业发达的
名词（复数）：工业股票；工业公司

forms.label: 无变化（形容词无词形变化）

由 industrial 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「使工业化」
由 industrialize 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「工业化」

senses.title: Relating to factories
senses.definition: connected with factories and the making of goods in large numbers
senses.definitionCN: 与工厂以及大批量制造商品有关
senses.example: Industrial waste must be treated before it leaves the plant.
senses.exampleCN: 工业废料在出厂之前必须经过处理。
senses.why: The adjective simply attaches the noun industry to whatever it describes.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把名词 industry 挂到它所修饰的对象上。

senses.title: Having many industries
senses.definition: having a strong economy based on factories and manufacturing
senses.definitionCN: 经济以工厂与制造业为基础的
senses.example: The north of the country is heavily industrial.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家的北部高度工业化。
senses.why: A place can be filled with industry, so the adjective describes its character.
senses.whyCN: 一个地方可以被工业填满，于是这个形容词也描述它的性质。

senses.title: Of a whole sector
senses.titleCN: 产业的：指整个行业层面
senses.definition: belonging to an entire branch of production rather than one workshop
senses.definitionCN: 属于整个生产门类，而不是单个作坊
senses.example: The report looks at industrial policy across the region.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告考察整个地区的产业政策。
senses.why: From single factories the word rises to the level of policy and sectors.
senses.whyCN: 从单个工厂出发，这个词上升到政策和行业层面。

senses.title: Of the machine age
senses.definition: belonging to the period when machines replaced handwork
senses.definitionCN: 属于机器取代手工劳动的那个时期
senses.example: The industrial age changed how people lived and worked.
senses.exampleCN: 工业时代改变了人们的居住与工作方式。
senses.why: Industrial also names an era, because factories reorganized all of life.
senses.whyCN: industrial 也命名一个时代，因为工厂重组了整个生活。

intro.en: Industrial is the adjective of industry, which comes from Latin industria, meaning diligence, the quality of working hard.
intro.cn: industrial 是 industry 的形容词形式，而 industry 来自拉丁语 industria，意为「勤勉」，即努力工作的品质。

items.en: Industria was built from indu, or in, plus struere, to build.
items.cn: industria 由 indu（或 in）加 struere（建造）构成。

items.en: The sense was activity or diligence, and it could also name a trade.
items.cn: 其义为活动或勤勉，也可指一门行业。

items.en: Industrie reached English through French with both senses kept.
items.cn: industrie 经法语进入英语，两种含义都被保留。

items.en: During the eighteenth century industry came to mean manufacturing at scale.
items.cn: 十八世纪 industry 开始指大规模的制造业。

items.en: The adjective industrial was formed to describe everything factories touched.
items.cn: 形容词 industrial 被造出来，描述工厂所触及的一切。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words sharing the industria root; the near-meaning group holds adjectives for factories and working life.
note.cn: 形近组收共享 industria 词根的词；近义组收与工厂和劳动有关的形容词。

entries.definition: The making of goods in factories, or a trade.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「工业；行业；勤奋」，是工业一词根的名词。

entries.definition: Working hard and steadily.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「勤劳的」，只是拼写相近，含义偏向勤奋。

entries.definition: Having developed manufacturing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「已工业化的」，由 industrialize 变来。

entries.definition: The business of making goods in factories.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「制造业」，强调制造过程。

entries.definition: Connected with trade and profit.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「商业的」，强调买卖而非生产。

entries.definition: Worked by machinery.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「机械的」，强调机器运转本身。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the industria root, the -al adjective ending and the familiar phrase industrial revolution.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 industria 词根、形容词后缀 -al 以及熟悉的短语 industrial revolution。

normal.en: Industry plus -al gives an adjective: whatever is industrial belongs to industry.
normal.cn: industry 加 -al 得到形容词：industrial 修饰的东西都属于工业。

normal.en: Industria meant diligence in Latin, so industry first meant hard work, then the work itself.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 industria 意为勤勉，所以 industry 先指努力，再指所做的事。

normal.en: Industrialize adds -ize to make a verb, so a country can be industrialized.
normal.cn: industrialize 加上 -ize 成了动词，所以说一个国家可以工业化。

normal.en: Industrial area and industrial waste both say what the word describes.
normal.cn: industrial area 与 industrial waste 都说明了这个词描述的是什么。

normal.en: Do not confuse industrial with industrious: factories against hardworking people.
normal.cn: 不要把 industrial 与 industrious 混淆：一个是工厂，一个是勤劳的人。

abstract.en: Industry is diligence made visible: pipes, chimneys and night shifts.
abstract.cn: 工业是看得见的勤勉：管道、烟囱与夜班。

abstract.en: Industrial is a scale word, not a place word; it describes eras and policies.
abstract.cn: industrial 是尺度的词，不是地点的词；它描述时代与政策。

abstract.en: Smoke is the quickest picture: wherever it rises in rows, the word fits.
abstract.cn: 烟是最快的画面：凡成排升起之处，这个词就用得上。

examples.en: The industrial part of the city is grey with smoke.
examples.cn: 城市的工业区被烟雾染成灰色。

examples.en: Industrial growth brought jobs to the small town.
examples.cn: 工业增长给这个小镇带来了工作。

examples.en: They studied industrial design at a technical college.
examples.cn: 他们在一所技术学院学习工业设计。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬打湿」——厂房里的机器硬打湿了工人的衣服。

root: 拉丁语 industria（勤勉）= indu/in（在内）+ struere（建造）；同族词有 industry、industrious、industrialize。

sensesIntro.en: From the diligence inside industria, industrial grows into an adjective for factories, for regions full of them, for whole sectors and for a historical age.
sensesIntro.cn: 从 industria 中的勤勉之义出发，industrial 发展为描述工厂、工业密集的地区、整个产业以及一个历史时代的形容词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rows of chimneys working through the night.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排排烟囱通宵工作。

branches.en: FACTORY LINE: waste, machines and goods belong to the plant.
branches.cn: 工厂线：废料、机器与货物都属于厂区。

branches.en: REGION LINE: a whole area can be filled with industry.
branches.cn: 地区线：整片区域可以被工业填满。

branches.en: SECTOR LINE: policy looks at the industry as a whole.
branches.cn: 产业线：政策着眼于作为整体的产业。

branches.en: TIME LINE: the machine age gets its name from the same root.
branches.cn: 时间线：机器时代也从同一词根得名。

branches.en: OUTPUT LINE: what a factory and a sector produce is one flow of goods.
branches.cn: 产出线：工厂与产业生产的东西是同一条货物流。

intro.en: An adjective built on a Latin noun, with suffixes that make verbs and nouns from it.
intro.cn: 一个建立在拉丁名词之上的形容词，并由此再生出动词与名词形式。

latinIntro.en: The root struere, to build, also yields structure and construct, which is why industria means diligence.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 struere 意为建造，也产生了 structure 与 construct，这也是 industria 意为勤勉的原因。

definition_zh: 工业；产业；行业；勤奋
definition_en: the making of goods in factories, a branch of trade, or steady hard work
core_image: 一片厂区里机器不停，工人在流水线旁忙碌
scene: 城市的经济账全写在一个个行业里。The car industry provides thousands of jobs in this region.
sceneCN: 这里 industry 是「行业、产业」（第 1 个义项：生产商品的一个门类）；句意是汽车产业在这个地区提供了数千个工作岗位。

pos.zh: 名词：工业；产业；行业；勤奋

derivatives.zh: 加 -al 构成形容词，义为「工业的」
加 -ious 构成形容词，义为「勤劳的」
加动词后缀构成，义为「使工业化」
